parts.label: b

A coin is selected at random and tossed.

Given that the coin that was tossed comes up heads, what is the probability that it was the fair coin?

solutions.latex: Amplitude $3$ and vertical shift $4$, so $y$ ranges from $4-3=1$ to $4+3=7$: $[1,7]$. Answer C.
The graph of $x=y^2+1$ is a parabola opening to the right: each $x>1$ gives two values of $y$. So one to many. Answer C.
$P(B|A)=\dfrac{P(B\cap A)}{P(A)}$ gives $\sqrt{p}=\dfrac{P(B\cap A)}{p}$, so $P(B\cap A)=p^{3/2}$. Then $P(A|B)=\dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}=\dfrac{p^{3/2}}{p^2}=p^{-1/2}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{p}}$. Answer D.
$\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-2x\right)=\cos 2x$, which is an even function, so the distribution is symmetric about $x=0$. Hence $P(X>0.2)=P(X<-0.2)$. Answer B.

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{x}$, so $m=\dfrac{1}{a}$. At $x=e$ the gradient is $\dfrac{1}{e}$ and at $x=1$ it is $1$; since $1<a<e$, $\dfrac{1}{e}<m<1$. The tangent at $x=e$ has $c=0$ and the tangent at $x=1$ has $c=-1$, so for the tangent at $x=a$, $-1<c<0$. Answer A.

Let $u=\tan x,\ v=e^{2x}$, so $u'=\sec^2 x,\ v'=2e^{2x}$.

The line is $x=5-y$. Area $=\displaystyle\int_2^5(5-y)\,dy+\int_1^2(-y^2+6y-5)\,dy=\left[5y-\dfrac{y^2}{2}\right]_2^5+\left[-\dfrac{y^3}{3}+3y^2-5y\right]_1^2=\dfrac{25}{2}-8+\left(-\dfrac23\right)-\left(-\dfrac73\right)=4\dfrac12+\dfrac53=\dfrac{37}{6}$ units$^2$ ($6\dfrac16$).

Alternatively: area of triangle $BCD$ (with $D(0,2)$) $=\dfrac12\times3\times3=\dfrac92$, plus $\displaystyle\int_1^2(-y^2+6y-5)\,dy=\dfrac53$, total $\dfrac{37}{6}$.

From the 45 degree angles, the horizontal extension at each end equals $h$ (since $\tan45^\circ=\dfrac{h}{x}$ gives $x=h$), so the top width is $b=a+2h$.

Area $=\dfrac12h(a+b)$: $60=\dfrac12h(2a+2h)$, $120=2ah+2h^2$, $a=\dfrac{120}{2h}-\dfrac{2h^2}{2h}=\dfrac{60}{h}-h$.

$A=60h^{-1}-h+2h\sqrt2+120$, $\dfrac{dA}{dh}=-60h^{-2}-1+2\sqrt2$, $\dfrac{d^2A}{dh^2}=\dfrac{120}{h^3}$.

$v=0$ when the engine stops: $0=0.5e^t\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{10}\right)$. Since $0.5e^t\neq0$ (no solution), $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{10}\right)=0$, so $\dfrac{\pi t}{10}=0,\pi,2\pi,\ldots$ and $\dfrac{t}{10}=0,1,2,\ldots$

solutions.latex:
$\dfrac{dv}{dt}=0.5e^t\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{10}\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{10}\right)+0.5e^t\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{10}\right)=0.5e^t\left(\dfrac{\pi}{10}\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{10}+\sin\dfrac{\pi t}{10}\right)$.

Setting $\dfrac{dv}{dt}=0$ (as $0.5e^t\neq0$): $\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{10}\right)=-\dfrac{\pi}{10}$, so $\dfrac{\pi t}{10}=2.837\ldots$ and $t=2.837\ldots\times\dfrac{10}{\pi}\approx9.03$ seconds.
